quotes.quote: High-quality sequencing data were generated, followed by computational subtraction of human host sequences mapping to the human reference genome (hg19) using Kraken2 2.1.2 and Burrows-Wheeler Alignment (BWA). Low-quality and short reads (length < 50 bp) were removed by fastp 0.20.1.

The remaining data were aligned to the Pathogenic Microbial Genome Databases, including bacteria, viruses, fungi, and parasites. The classification reference databases were downloaded from National Center of Biotechnology Information (NCBI) ( ftp://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/ ) and the mapped data were processed for advanced analysis.

At least two reads were mapped to the pathogens, except for specific pathogens such as Bacillus anthracis, Orientia tsutsugamushi, Chlamydia pneumoniae, Brucella, Cryptococcus neoformans, Coronavirus, Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) , and Toxoplasma , whose relative abundances would be surpassed ( Formula ) ( Zhang et al., 2020 ).

Pathogens with the highest absolute abundance in their genus (Top 5) and (2) Species with relative abundance ≥ 5% for bacteria, ≥ 50% for fungi, and ≥ 10% for viruses, were considered dominant species.

method_quotes.quote: A 1.5–3 mL of the BALF sample or 5 mL of blood sample was collected from each patient. Nucleic acid extraction took place using a TIANamp Micro DNA Kit (DP316, Tiangen Biotech Co., Beijing, China).

Qualified libraries were sequenced by the Illumina 550 platform. (3) High-quality sequencing data were generated, followed by computational subtraction of human host sequences mapping to the human reference genome (hg19) using Kraken2 2.1.2 and Burrows-Wheeler Alignment (BWA).
The remaining data were aligned to the Pathogenic Microbial Genome Databases, including bacteria, viruses, fungi, and parasites.

At least two reads were mapped to the pathogens, except for specific pathogens such as Bacillus anthracis, Orientia tsutsugamushi, Chlamydia pneumoniae, Brucella, Cryptococcus neoformans, Coronavirus, Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) , and Toxoplasma , whose relative abundances would be surpassed ( Formula ) ( Zhang et al., 2020 ).

Pathogens with the highest absolute abundance in their genus (Top 5) and (2) Species with relative abundance ≥ 5% for bacteria, ≥ 50% for fungi, and ≥ 10% for viruses, were considered dominant species.

specification.input_notes: BioProject PRJNA865167 contains 20 SRA runs (SRR20749332–SRR20749351), corresponding to the 20 samples (13 BALF and 7 blood) from 15 patients used for the etiological/coinfection analysis. The paper states that 10 patients' mNGS fastq data were lost and excluded, so the deposit is the subset of raw sequencing reads available for the target analysis. No sample-to-run mapping is provided in the paper; the run accessions are the smallest sufficient input set.

specification.comparison_metric: Compare the reported mNGS positive detection proportion (13/13) and culture positive detection proportion (6/13) with the solver's recomputed counts from the deposited raw reads using the described mNGS pipeline and thresholds.
specification.numerical_agreement_criterion: Proportions compared by numerator/denominator: mNGS 13/13 and culture 6/13 must match exactly; the reported P < 0.05 is compared at the reported precision.
specification.specification_gaps: No mapping of the 20 SRA runs to the 20 samples/15 patients is given; the exact version of the NCBI pathogen reference database is not stated; the exact Kraken2/BWA/fastp parameters beyond read length <50 bp and the ≥2-read threshold are not fully specified; the formula for relative abundance is given but the exact denominator handling for bacteria/fungi/viruses/parasites is not fully detailed; the culture method details and how the 13 culture-tested samples were selected are not fully described.
